profile.name: Bharat Forge Ltd
profile.what: India's largest forging company: crankshafts, connecting rods, front axle beams, steering knuckles and transmission parts for trucks and cars (India and exports), plus forgings for oil & gas, construction and mining, rail, large engines (data-centre and power-gen sets), aerospace and semiconductors. Defence through Kalyani Strategic Systems (KSSL, 100%): artillery (ATAGS), protected vehicles, small arms, ammunition shells, naval gas-turbine generators. Overseas forging and aluminium plants in Germany, Sweden, France, Italy and the US; K Drive (ex-AAM India axles) and JS Autocast (castings) in India.
profile.facilities: 36 manufacturing facilities (28 in India, 6 in Europe, 2 in the US) at 30-Jun-2026
profile.revenueMixFY26: Consolidated revenue Rs16,812 cr: India 31%, Europe 36%, USA 23%, others 10% by customer location (AR FY26 note 49); 67% made in India

orders._note: Rs cr, Q1FY27 wins and Jun-2026 defence order book

callPoints: Standalone margin 26.2% bore ~160bp of energy, input and logistics cost increases (Iran war, LPG crisis); ~28% normalised. Recoveries are being negotiated and will lift revenue and cost together, so the margin improves gradually (CFO, Kedar Dixit).

CDP Bharat Forge (German steel forging) restructuring on track: closure by Q3 CY2027; a ~EUR30 mn (~Rs330 cr) manpower-redundancy provision taken in Q1, paid out over 6-12 months; part of CDP's orders move to India.

US steel forging had ~3 months without production after press breakdowns (EBITDA -Rs4 cr); fixed, recovery in Q2. Target margins ~12% (steel) and 15-16% (aluminium) "hopefully next year", but the 50% US tariff on Canadian aluminium is the obstacle.

Defence: largest naval order so far (12 marine gas-turbine generator sets for the Navy); new defence facility enters serial production this year for ATAGS and CQB carbines; ATAGS start waits for FOPM approval ("a few weeks of delay"). Steady-state defence EBITDA margin target 22-23%.
Aerospace ~Rs400 cr, to double in ~2 years (Baramati ring mill from Q4FY27); semiconductor components USD30-40 mn in 2 years; energy/data-centre business to double in four years.

Board approved a fund raise of up to Rs2,500 cr for ~Rs1,800 cr of growth capex over 12-18 months (forging, ring rolling, machining; energetics plant in Andhra Pradesh) and possible Indian M&A; asset turn above 1.5x. Manpower back to 70-75% of normal.
Outlook: FY27 growth of 20-25% for the India manufacturing business, more pronounced in H2; FY28 "should also be a strong year".
